gates.claim: hexp: exp(F) = prod_j(1 - x*y_j)/x = 1 on the arc (and prod_j(1 - y_j/x) = 1/x) -- ALREADY Lean-proved as prod_one_sub_x_mul / prod_x_sub; measured only to confirm the instantiation is the one the lemma expects
h0: F(0) = Sum_j Log(1 - y_j) = 0 at the base point x = 1 -- this is what selects the integer 0 rather than merely showing it is constant

the ONLY contact with the cut on the whole arc is at the endpoint phi = pi, and it is TRANSVERSAL. (a) On [0, pi-0.2] the margin has an interior minimum of 0.337 at phi/pi = 0.542 -- a real local minimum, bounded well away from zero, so nothing crosses the cut inside. (b) On [0, pi-delta] for delta <= 0.05 the minimum moves to the right endpoint and equals w_1*delta, ratio -> 1 over 3 further orders of magnitude: linear collapse, not tangential

the factor that lands on the cut is exactly 1 - w_1 = -(w_1 - 1) = -1.2469796..., with w_1 the largest root of the level-7 ladder's own cubic w^3 - 2w^2 - w + 1. The arc's endpoint sitting on the cut is structural, not coincidental -- and x = -1 is on the cut as well

the branch point is invisible to the cut margin -- margin ~0.77 at phi_0, nowhere near zero. The cut condition and the collision condition are independent, which is exactly why the symmetric repair survives a branch point that killed the per-root argument

ORIENTATION IS LOAD-BEARING, and this is the mechanism behind the three spurious 2*pi's recorded on qou-trns. Rising to phi = pi the factor reaches -(w_1-1) from ABOVE, arg -> +pi, matching the principal branch's value ON the cut: F is continuous, hcont holds. Descending to phi = -pi it arrives from BELOW, arg -> -pi, while principal Log still returns +pi: a genuine 2*pi*i discontinuity at the endpoint
conclusion (this is what the lemma OUTPUTS, recorded so the instantiation is seen to close): F = Sum_j Log(1 - x*y_j) - i*phi vanishes on the arc -- branch integer 0, endpoint included

verdict.outcome: The branch-integer step is now a Lean theorem with its hypotheses separated: exp(F)=1 and F(0)=0 are already theorems (Vieta), and the only open input is continuity of F on [0, pi].
verdict.the_finding: the transport arc ENDS ON THE BRANCH CUT, twice over: x = -1 is on it, and the factor 1 - x*y_1 equals -(w_1 - 1) = -1.2469796 there, with w_1 the largest root of the level-7 ladder's cubic. The first version of this probe tested 'no factor touches the cut' and failed at 9.3e-43; the condition was too strong, but the failure was real information.
verdict.why_hcont_still_holds: continuity forbids CROSSING the cut, not touching it. The contact is transversal (margin = w_1*(pi-phi), G3) and one-sided from above, and the principal branch's value on the cut is the limit from above. So F is continuous on [0, pi] and the lemma applies.
verdict.cause_of_the_recurring_2pi: G6. Rising through the endpoint the principal branch is continuous; descending through it, it jumps by 2*pi*i. qou-trns records three spurious 2*pi's and calls them the most reliable false alarm in this work; this is their mechanism, and it is structural.
verdict.still_not_proved: hcont is MEASURED, not proved. Proving it means showing from the curve that no factor 1 - x*y_j meets (-inf, 0] for phi in [0, pi), a real-algebraic statement, plus the one-sided limit at the endpoint. NOT written. Until it is, hcont is an assumption and the transport is open.
